sources.name: United Nations World Population Prospects (2024 Revision)
sources.organization: United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division
sources.description: Historical population series 1950-2023, medium fertility projections through 2100, crude birth rates, crude death rates, and life expectancy.
sources.citation: United Nations, Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division (2024). World Population Prospects 2024.

sources.name: Global Carbon Budget 2024
sources.description: Global fossil and land-use CO2 emissions, atmospheric concentrations (Mauna Loa / NOAA), ocean and land carbon sinks.
sources.citation: Friedlingstein et al. (2024). Global Carbon Budget 2024. Earth System Science Data.

sources.name: NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory Atmospheric CO2 Observations
sources.organization: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA ESRL / GML)
sources.description: In-situ continuous atmospheric CO2 mole fractions measured at Mauna Loa Observatory, Hawaii from 1958 through present.
sources.citation: NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory (2026). Trends in Atmospheric Carbon Dioxide. NOAA/GML, Boulder, Colorado.

sources.name: NASA GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (GISTEMP v4)
sources.organization: NASA Goddard Institute for Space Studies
sources.description: Global surface temperature anomalies combining GHCNv4 meteorological stations and ERSSTv5 sea surface temperatures.
sources.citation: GISTEMP Team (2025). GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (GISTEMP), version 4. NASA Goddard Institute for Space Studies.

sources.name: Copernicus Climate Change Service (ECMWF ERA5 Reanalysis)
sources.organization: European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF)
sources.description: Fifth-generation ECMWF global climate reanalysis covering 1940 through present with hourly 2m air temperature, ocean heat content, and sea ice anomalies.
sources.citation: Hersbach et al. (2020). The ERA5 global reanalysis. Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society, 146(730), 1999-2049.

sources.name: Our World in Data Open Data Catalog (CO2, Energy, Demography)
sources.organization: Global Change Data Lab / University of Oxford
sources.description: Harmonized global and country-level time series integrating BP, Ember, UN, World Bank, and Global Carbon Project.
sources.citation: Ritchie, Roser, & Rosado (2024). Energy and CO2 Emissions. Our World in Data.

sources.name: World Energy Outlook 2024 & Energy and AI Report
sources.license: Terms of Use / Non-commercial academic research
sources.description: Global energy generation, fossil vs renewable shares, grid carbon intensities, data center electricity demand.
sources.citation: IEA (2024). World Energy Outlook 2024. International Energy Agency, Paris.

sources.name: Ember Global Electricity Review (2024-2026)
sources.description: Yearly and monthly clean electricity shares, solar/wind capacity, thermal power emissions, and grid decarbonization trajectories.
sources.citation: Ember (2024). Global Electricity Review 2024. Ember Climate Analytics.

sources.name: Planetary Boundaries Assessment (2023 Update & 2025/2026 Transgression Updates)
sources.organization: Stockholm Resilience Centre & Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research
sources.description: Control variables, thresholds, and current status for all 9 Earth System boundaries, including the recent transgression assessment of ocean acidification.
sources.citation: Richardson et al. (2023). Earth beyond six of nine planetary boundaries. Science Advances 9, eadh2458.

sources.name: World Bank World Development Indicators
sources.description: Global GDP (constant USD), manufacturing value added, industrial capital formation, inequality metrics, and fertility rates.

sources.name: FAOSTAT Food and Agriculture Database
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.description: Global arable land, cereal yield per hectare, agricultural fertilizer consumption (N, P, K), food production index.

sources.name: WRI Aqueduct Water Risk Atlas 4.0
sources.description: Global hydrological catchments assessing baseline water stress, interannual supply variability, and industrial/cooling water competition.
sources.citation: Kuzma, S. et al. (2023). Aqueduct 4.0: Updated Decision-Relevant Global Water Risk Metrics. World Resources Institute.

sources.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries (2024-2026)
sources.organization: U.S. Geological Survey (National Minerals Information Center)
sources.description: Annual worldwide reserves, primary extraction, and secondary recycling metrics for copper, lithium, cobalt, nickel, and rare earth elements.
sources.citation: U.S. Geological Survey (2024). Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024: U.S. Geological Survey, 212 p.

sources.name: Epoch AI & SemiAnalysis AI Hardware & Compute Frontier Database
sources.description: Historical and projected compute capacity (FP16/BF16 EFLOPS), accelerator fleet shipments, cluster utilization, and energy consumption.
sources.citation: Epoch (2024). Parameter and Compute Trends in Artificial Intelligence. Epoch AI Research.

sources.name: Exploring the Viability of the Updated World3 Model for Examining the Impact of Computing on Planetary Boundaries
sources.description: System dynamics formulation of AI data center capital share, CO2 emissions, e-waste intensity, and persistent pollution in World3-03.
sources.citation: Guliyeva, N., Bhardwaj, E., & Becker, C. (2025). LIMITS '25 / arXiv:2510.07634.

sources.name: IIASA Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP) Database v2
sources.organization: International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis (IIASA)
sources.description: Harmonized global and 5/10/32 region socioeconomic and emissions trajectories for SSP1 through SSP5 used in IPCC AR6.
sources.citation: Riahi, K. et al. (2017). The Shared Socioeconomic Pathways and their energy, land use, and greenhouse gas emissions implications. Global Environmental Change.
